text: Quick SEO check you can do in 10 seconds: open your homepage, view source, search for <title>. If it's missing, empty, or the same on every page, that's the first thing to fix.
Many sites block AI crawlers without knowing it. A single "Disallow: /" under "User-agent: *" in robots.txt also stops GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot. Worth checking once.
Meta descriptions don't directly affect rankings, but they often become the snippet people read before clicking. Aim for roughly 120-160 characters and write it for humans.
Agencies: the question "why doesn't ChatGPT ever mention us?" is coming up in client calls. The first thing to check is boring but common: robots.txt blocking GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot or PerplexityBot.

Noindex by accident is one of the most expensive SEO mistakes, and it hides in two places: the meta robots tag and the X-Robots-Tag HTTP header. Check both on every page.
Many sites block AI crawlers with a broad rule they added years ago for a different reason. Blocking training bots and blocking AI search bots are separate decisions. Audit before you decide.

Duplicate titles and missing meta descriptions are the most common issues on small business sites. They're also the quickest wins to show a new client in week one.
Structured data (JSON-LD) is one of the clearest signals for both rich results and AI answers. The audit lists which schema types each page uses, so gaps are easy to spot.

Thin pages rarely rank and rarely get cited by AI answers. Merge them, expand them, or noindex them. A crawl that flags low word counts makes the list for you.
Missing Open Graph tags make every shared link look broken on social apps. It's a two-minute fix that clients notice immediately.
